name: Individual Nanoplastic Particle Raman Spectra (Xie et al. 2023)
description: Raman spectra of 1,000 individual nanoplastic particles for polymer classification: 200 each of PE (polyethylene), PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate), PS (polystyrene), PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) and PVC (polyvinyl chloride) (Xie et al. 2023, Environ. Sci. Technol. 57(46):18203-18214, doi:10.1021/acs.est.3c03210). Particles (300 nm - 1 um) were dried onto polished aluminum sheets (95% reflectivity) and measured with an XploRA Plus confocal Raman spectrometer (HORIBA Jobin Yvon) at 532 nm (external-cavity diode laser, ~10 mW at the sample = 10% of the 100 mW output) through a x100 Olympus objective; 500-1,799 cm^-1 at 467 points (2-3 cm^-1 grid, identical axis in every file). Each .txt file in the deposit is one particle; the deposit additionally holds 200 BLANK substrate spectra (aluminum background, no particle), which are excluded here. Spectra are raw counts as deposited (no blank subtraction, no normalization). The single-particle SNR regime makes this a harder, noisier identification task than any bulk microplastics set; the paper's pipeline (peak extraction and retention + random forest) reached 98.8% average accuracy.

rai:dataBiases: Data were acquired under controlled laboratory conditions and may not generalise to field or clinical settings. rai:dataLimitations: Reference spectra represent ideal laboratory conditions; real-world samples may show additional interference from impurities, fluorescence, or surface effects.
